<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx`  _(via IApprovalService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class), IApprovalService (symbol, a top-level interface), approvals.getRecordLock (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/approvals/records/:object/:recordId/lock, selected by route anchor /approvals/records/:object/:recordId/lock), approvals.getRecordLocks (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/approvals/records/:object/locks, selected by route anchor /approvals/records/:object/locks), getRecordLock (sdk, the bare tail of client method approvals.getRecordLock, bound to GET /api/v1/approvals/records/:object/:recordId/lock), getRecordLocks (sdk, the bare tail of client method approvals.getRecordLocks, bound to POST /api/v1/approvals/records/:object/locks), /approvals/records/:object/:recordId/lock (route, bridged from symbol getRecordLock — its route source's handler names it; bridged from symbol recordLockPayload — its route source's handler names it), /approvals/records/:object/locks (route, bridged from symbol getRecordLocks — its route source's handler names it; bridged from symbol recordLockPayload — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via /approvals/records/:object/:recordId/lock (route, bridged from symbol getRecordLock — its route source's handler names it; bridged from symbol recordLockPayload — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc3ec37a669f1b80c393e31393caea49fb4f7b09` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a9e4e9a765f715fa249a3e25a404904ca1dd552a` — the merge of head `030cd914ca876896bf487e2a01efaf24aeba3b37` into base `bc3ec37a669f1b80c393e31393caea49fb4f7b09`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a9e4e9a765f715fa249a3e25a404904ca1dd552a && git checkout a9e4e9a765f715fa249a3e25a404904ca1dd552a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bc3ec37a669f1b80c393e31393caea49fb4f7b09 030cd914ca876896bf487e2a01efaf24aeba3b37 && git checkout -B drift-repro bc3ec37a669f1b80c393e31393caea49fb4f7b09 && git merge --no-ff 030cd914ca876896bf487e2a01efaf24aeba3b37

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc3ec37a669f1b80c393e31393caea49fb4f7b09
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bc3ec37a669f1b80c393e31393caea49fb4f7b09` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e99cf2cfdea67ae14b2d5218f32618df96a10293`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts

Inputs read: card #37151 body and all eight comments (triage 7146843018, anchor item 7148285178, rulings 7148474531 and 7148480184, triage 7148580286, claim 7150121798, dev reports 7151644818 and 7152480071); PR #37191 body, file list and net diff against `main` (merge base a10345ab); the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `lifecycle-hooks.ts` (`recordHeldByLockingApproval`, `detailRowsHeldByLockingApproval`, `lockingRequestsForRecords`, `pendingRequestFor`, `bindDetailRowLockHook`), `record-page-routes.ts`, `rest-route-ledger.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`IApprovalService.getRecordLock` / `getRecordLocks` return types gain `lockSource?: 'record' | 'master'`.** Right, and a pure widening: the field is optional, no export is added, an implementation answering `{ locked }` alone still type-checks, and every in-tree caller outside the diff reads `locked` alone (`record-page-routes.ts`, `service-storage/record-file-access.ts`).
- **REST wire, both doors.** Right. A locked entry gains one field; an unlocked entry, the 404 and the batch `locked: null` entry are byte-for-byte what `main` serves. `recordLockPayload` keeps `locked: lock.locked === true` semantics and serves `lockSource` only from the closed pair, so nothing an implementation adds reaches the wire. No request accept-set moves: the closed query sets and the `recordIds` body key are untouched. No published response schema names these routes (the route ledger rows carry no shape), so nothing else is owed.
- **Client SDK types.** Right: both answers widen with the same optional field (see ④).
- **`locked` itself is unchanged at both doors.** Right. Batch: `held.has(id) || heldByMaster.has(id)` became `recordLockAnswer(heldByMaster.has(id), held.has(id))`, the same truth value; the detail check now runs over every readable id instead of the unheld ones, same number of reads. Single: the two judgements run in the other order, same truth value.
- **Readability anchors.** Right as built: the single door's anchor is the `main` text unchanged (any returned row), the batch door's is unchanged (the row whose id is the asked id). No published answer narrows, so no `(narrowing)` arm is owed.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`.** Right: nothing a metadata author can write changes.
- **Gates.** Every check-run on the head concluded `success` or `skipped`; none failed, none pending. Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, the Type Check families, Test Core 1 to 10 and the Dogfood Regression Gate are among the successes.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening: both lock doors' published entry gains a field)` is the right line and the right arm: a published return type and two wire answers gain an optional field, nothing is taken away. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. Under AGENTS.md (changeset rule 3: the level follows the kind alone; `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`) `patch` is the correct level, not `minor`. The changeset names all four packages the diff publishes from (`@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/client`) and carries both declaration lines line-initial, as the PR body does. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Round-1 open question 1 (client type, record-page composite, skill sentence).** Answered. The client type is in this diff. The composite is carried by card #37195. The skill sentence ("`locked` and nothing else") is routed to triage per the PR body; I found no card naming it, so the seat confirms its carrier before merge. Neither is in this diff, and neither is made wrong on the wire by it (the composite keeps serving `{ locked }`).
- **Round-1 open question 2 (is a narrowing arm owed for the anchor alignment).** Answered by removal: head e99cf2cf restores the single door's anchor, so nothing narrows and the widening arm stands alone.
- **Anchor item 7148285178, escalated to the seat (record, not code).** Ruling record 7148480184 and triage 7148580286 both say the anchor is aligned in this change with a parity pin. The head does the opposite, on a "seat ruling on PR #37191" that the spec docblock, the plugin docblocks, the route comment and the changeset all cite, and that exists nowhere as a comment with an id: its only trace is the edited footer of claim 7150121798. Not aligning is the right call on the merits (the only alignment one `$in` read allows is the strict one, which turns a served answer into a 404, a narrowing nobody ruled). But `Fixes #37151` closes the card with that row unticked. Owed before merge, on the card: the seat's ruling as a comment of its own, and the row either ticked as "kept different, on purpose" or moved to a carrier.
- **Dev's unfiled inference (write hook keyed on the writer's spelling of the id), corroborated by reading, escalated.** `pendingRequestFor` matches `sys_approval_request.record_id` against the id exactly as asked, at the write hook and at both reads. On a driver that matches a row under a looser spelling than that text column does, a by-id update could miss the lock. Outside this diff and not changed by it; it is a lock-bypass shape, so it deserves a card and a measured probe rather than "noted, not filed". Finding S1 below is the read-side face of the same fact.
- **SQL push-down.** No finding. The diff adds no read and no id materialisation: the batch door's detail check takes `readableAsked` where it took the unheld subset, still `1 + edges` bounded reads under the 200-id cap, and the in-app judgement has its stated reason (`node_config_json` snapshot, the write hook's own judgement) in `detailRowsHeldByLockingApproval`'s docblock.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` (hits), against ruling 7148480184 and its first consumer (the grid row menu, #36911).** The revised "What is answered" bullet states the ruling exactly: `locked`, `lockSource` only on a locked answer, `'record'` and `'master'` defined by the two existing judgements, master wins when both hold, `{ locked: false }` with no kind, `null` unchanged, no request id, node, participants or `pending`. The revision of the #25934 sentence is cited to the ruling that made it. The field name follows the claim's measured precedent (`lockSource` in `api/protocol.zod.ts`). The consumer's need (hide Delete where the server refuses it) is met by `'master'` winning: the detail-row hook refuses a line's delete whenever a master is held, whatever the line's own request.

Cases, both doors, read against `approval-service.ts` and `lifecycle-hooks.ts` at the head:

| Case | Single door | Batch door | Agrees with the docblock |
|---|---|---|---|
| readable, held by its own request only | `{ locked: true, lockSource: 'record' }` | same | yes |
| readable line, master held only | `{ locked: true, lockSource: 'master' }` | same | yes |
| readable line, both held | `'master'` (master asked first) | `'master'` (`recordLockAnswer` tests master first) | yes |
| readable, own request on a non-locking node, master unheld | `{ locked: false }` | same | yes |
| readable, unlocked | `{ locked: false }`, no `lockSource` | same | yes |
| unreadable | `null`, returned before any lock read | `null`; the id never reaches a lock read | yes |
| missing, blank id, object read refused | `null` | `null` at each position | yes |
| repeated id | n/a | answered at each position | yes |
| loose spelling, line of a held master | `'master'` | `null` | yes |
| loose spelling, held by its own request | `{ locked: false }` (see S1) | `null` | **no** |

S1 (should-fix) — the batch docblock's new sentence "an id the engine matches under another spelling answers `null` here and the lock there" is not what the single door does for a record held by its own request. `getRecordLock` passes the id as asked to `recordHeldByLockingApproval`, which matches `sys_approval_request.record_id` against that exact string (`pendingRequestFor`); only the master half is judged off the row the engine found. So a self-held record asked as `'07'` for a numeric `7` (one of the two examples the docblock itself names), or in another letter case on a store whose bookkeeping column compares exactly, is readable, is held, and answers `{ locked: false }`. In the PR's own rig (ids folded on the business objects only) a self-held `held_sheet` asked in upper case would answer unlocked; the new pin covers the master-held line alone. The behaviour is `main`'s and this diff does not change it, which is why it is not a must-fix; the sentence is new, sits in the published contract, and promises the wrong direction for a lock read (unlocked for a held record). Fix, either: (a) say what is true: at the single door a loosely spelled id is judged for its master's lock off the row found and for its own lock off the id as asked, so a self-held record may answer `{ locked: false }`, and callers send ids as the server spelled them; the changeset and `approvals.mdx` ("answers its lock") follow; or (b) judge the row's own lock off the id the caller's read handed back, with a pin for the self-held loose case. (b) changes a served answer from `false` to `true` and belongs with the write-hook card in ③; (a) is the fix that fits this PR. Read from code, not run; no public entry was shown to send such an id.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`.** Agrees with the contract in every row above but the last. `recordLockAnswer` is the one spelling both doors use, so they cannot order the two kinds differently. The single door asks the master first and skips the own-request lookup when the master holds; the batch door now asks the detail lock of every readable id, which is what makes "both held" answer `'master'` there too. Disclosure: `heldByMaster` and `held` are consulted only for ids in `readableIds`, and the single door returns `null` before any SYSTEM read, so an unreadable or missing row learns nothing, and the two `null`s stay indistinguishable in shape and in reads issued. The docblocks' statements about readability (any returned row at the single door, the row whose id is the asked id at the batch door) are true of the code.

**`packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts`.** Agrees. Both doors serve through `recordLockPayload`: `locked !== true` gives `{ locked: false }` with no kind even if an implementation supplies one; a locked answer carries `lockSource` only when it is exactly `'record'` or `'master'`; anything else is dropped, never guessed. The batch door spreads that payload beside `recordId` and keeps `{ recordId, locked: null }` for a `null` answer; the single door keeps the one 404 for both `null`s, and 501 without the member. The route comments say this.

**`packages/client/src/index.ts`.** Agrees with the wire. Single: `{ locked: boolean; lockSource?: 'record' | 'master' }`. Batch entry: `{ recordId: string; locked: boolean | null; lockSource?: 'record' | 'master' }`, which admits all three served shapes (locked with kind, locked without kind from an older implementation, `locked: null` with none). Optional on both, matching a server that may omit it.

**Disclosure against #8652 ruling 5299823744 and ruling 7148480184.** Within the bound. The answer is served only to a caller who has just read the row as themselves. What is new is one bit on a locked row. `'master'` tells a line reader that some record the line belongs to is under a locking approval: before, `locked: true` on a line said that or "its own request", so the new bit removes that ambiguity and nothing more; this is the disclosure the maintainer ruled in ("the only extra disclosure is the lock's origin", master wins when both hold). It does not say which master (a line with several `master_detail` edges answers the same), which request, which node or who decides. `'record'` on a line implies its masters are unheld, which `{ locked: false }` on a sibling line already said. No path serves the bit for an unreadable row.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):
- nit — the contract docblock says `lockSource` is answered on a locked record but never that a conforming implementation may omit it; only the optional type, the REST comment and the changeset say so. One clause ("an implementation may answer a locked record without it; read an absent kind as unknown") would tell the first consumer what to do. Left as an accepted deviation or folded into the S1 edit.
- nit — both docblocks cite "seat ruling on PR #37191" with no comment id, unlike every other ruling they cite. Fixed on the record side by the comment ③ asks for.
- nit — `client.approvals.getRecordLock`'s docblock breaks its sentence as "— and / nothing else" after the inserted clause; it reads, but awkwardly.

S1 (should-fix) is open on this head. No must-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37151-lock-source-field`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgv2LZN1W2qSYTZvYs`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — REWORK · repo:objectstack#3 · head e99cf2cf · 2026-11-25T04:12Z

L1: REWORK (L1-w, zone wf-B)
Head-sha: `e99cf2cfdea67ae14b2d5218f32618df96a10293`

The L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this head is PASS, with one should-fix open: comment 7152618670, claim 7152536669. I add one should-fix of my own. Under the merge standard, both are fixed and re-read before landing, so this head is REWORK. This is Tier S: no governed path, 528 changed lines. wf-B lands it after ACCEPT.

### Should-fix

- **L2 S1 (adopted). The new batch docblock sentence says the single door answers "the lock there" for a loosely spelled id. That is false for a record held by its own request.** I checked it on the tree. `getRecordLock` reads the row with `where: { id }`, then judges the master half with `detailRowHeldByLockingApproval(…, id)`, and its own half with `recordHeldByLockingApproval(…, id)`, keyed on the id **as asked**. So a readable, self-held record asked as `'07'` for `7` answers `{ locked: false }`. The behaviour is `main`'s, but the sentence is new and published. The same claim is in the changeset ("answers its lock at the single-record door") and in `approvals.mdx`. Fix it the L2's way (a): state the truth in all three texts. The behaviour change (b) belongs with a separate card.
- **L1 S2. `Fixes #37151` closes the card while its anchor row is not disposed on the card.** Row 7148285178 asked for the two doors' readability anchors to be aligned, and ruling record 7148480184 and triage 7148580286 read it that way. The head keeps the anchors different, on the seat's 03:12Z ruling, and that is right on the merits: aligning them would narrow a served answer. But the ruling exists only as an edited footer on claim 7150121798, and the texts cite it as "seat ruling on PR #37191" with no comment id. Before landing:
  - the seat posts that ruling as its own comment on #37151 (or on this PR);
  - the row is ticked or carried to a card;
  - the three texts cite the comment id (that also closes L2 nit N2).

### Nits (in the L2 record)

- The docblock never says an implementation may omit `lockSource` on a locked answer. The changeset says it, and `recordLockPayload` serves `{ locked: true }` alone.
- The ruling citation has no comment id (folded into S2 above).
- One sentence break in the client docblock.

Fix them in the same push, or each needs a follow-up card.

### Read and found right (head e99cf2cf)

- `l1-face --pr 37191`: 13 items clean. Draft, base `main`. `Fixes #37151` binds only this card. `Clause-②: yes` (widening) · `Metadata-protocol: none`. The changeset names all four published packages moved: spec, plugin-approvals, rest and client. `patch` is right for a non-protocol widening (AGENTS.md). 62 success, 12 expected skips, 0 failed. `mergeable_state` was not computed at my read.
- **The contract, the doors and the client agree** on every other case:
  - `'record'`, `'master'`, `'master'` winning when both hold;
  - `{ locked: false }` with no kind;
  - `null`, folded to 404 or `locked: null`, never told apart.

  REST builds the payload field by field in `recordLockPayload`, so an implementation's extra fields are never served, and a kind-less locked answer is served `{ locked: true }`, never a guessed kind. The client types match all three wire shapes.
- **Disclosure.** The disclosure is one kind bit, served only after the caller's own read of the row, and never which master, request or approver. That is within ruling 7148480184 (option A, which revises the #25934 "`locked` only" text) and #8652 ruling 5299823744.
- **Changeset, sentence by sentence.** The two kinds and their delete rules, "`'master'` wins", the unchanged `null`, "No request id, node, approvers or `pending` flag", the optional member and the client sentence all hold. The one exception is the loose-spelling sentence (S1).
- The record-page composite (#37195) and the skills sentence went to triage on the seat's routing. Both are out of this PR's scope.

### Path to ACCEPT

1. Card thread: one push for S1's wording and S2's citation, plus any nits.
2. Seat: post the anchor ruling as its own comment, and tick or carry row 7148285178.
3. L1-w: a new claim, the same L2 reviewer reads the delta, and I read the L1 delta.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `030cd914ca876896bf487e2a01efaf24aeba3b37`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts

Delta record. It follows record 7152618670 on head e99cf2cf (PASS, S1 open) under claim 7152879550, and reads the one push e99cf2cf..030cd914 (7 files, 28 added, 15 removed). Inputs read this round: that delta; the card comments new since the first record (seat ruling 7152650156, triage 7152712740, dev report round 3 7152850913) and the mailbox request 7152670747 on #36743; the PR body; the check-runs on the new head. Everything the first record judged on e99cf2cf and this delta does not touch stands as judged there.

### ① Derived judgments

- **No behaviour moved.** Right. In the four scoped files every changed line is a docblock or comment line; no statement, signature or type changed. The other three files are the changeset body, `approvals.mdx` and two comments in the integration test. So every accept-set and public-surface judgement of record 7152618670 holds on this head unchanged: the two `IApprovalService` return types and the two client types widen by the optional `lockSource`, the REST doors serve it through `recordLockPayload`, `locked` is what `main` answers, and neither door's readability anchor moves.
- **Gates.** At the time of reading, the check-runs on this head stood at 29 success, 12 skipped, 30 in progress, none failed. The runs still in progress are Build Core, Type Check workspace, Type Check UI, Test Core 1 to 10, Test UI 1 to 16 and Build and E2E UI. A comment-only delta gives them nothing new to judge against e99cf2cf, where all of them were green, but their conclusions on this head are the gate verdicts and this record does not stand in for them: the merge waits for them.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and right. The delta leaves the changeset's front matter (four packages at `patch`) and both declaration lines untouched: `Clause-②: yes (widening: both lock doors' published entry gains a field)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. Under AGENTS.md changeset rule 3 a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The two reworded changeset paragraphs describe behaviour the tree has and publish nothing new.
